items.x: Dear Sam, Thanks for inviting me to your party on Saturday. Unfortunately, I can't come because my sister is getting married that day. Let's meet next week instead. Best, Leo
items.p: Why can't Leo go to the party?

items.x: Many people believe that working from home makes employees less productive. However, a recent study of 500 companies found that remote workers completed slightly more tasks, although they reported feeling more isolated from colleagues.
items.p: What did the study find?
o: Remote workers were slightly more productive but felt more isolated.

items.x: Urban beekeeping has surged in popularity, yet some ecologists warn that the trend may be counterproductive. Honeybees compete with wild pollinators for limited flowers, and in cities where hives are densely packed, native bee populations have been observed to decline.
items.p: What is the ecologists' main concern?
o: Honeybees may reduce the food available to wild bees.
Urban honey is unsafe to eat.

items.x: The author's insistence that the novel 'refuses easy consolation' is borne out by its ending: rather than reconciling the estranged brothers, it leaves them on opposite banks of the river, each convinced of his own innocence.
items.p: What does the ending suggest about the brothers?

items.x: Ostensibly a defence of fiscal prudence, the pamphlet in fact smuggles in a far more contentious premise: that public expenditure is inherently wasteful, a claim the author never troubles to substantiate.
items.p: What criticism is made of the pamphlet?
o: It relies on an unsupported assumption.
It argues for more public spending.

items.x: I was going to take the job in London, but in the end I turned it down. The salary was good, but I'd have had to commute for two hours a day.
items.p: Why did the speaker turn down the job?
o: The journey would have been too long.

items.x: Our quarterly results were better than expected, mainly thanks to online sales. That said, we can't ignore the fact that our high-street stores are still losing money.
items.p: What is the speaker's attitude?
o: Positive overall, but concerned about the physical stores.
Worried that online sales are falling.

items.x: I wouldn't go so far as to call the proposal a failure, but it's hard to see how it addresses the concerns residents raised at the last meeting.
items.p: What does the speaker imply?
o: The proposal doesn't respond well to residents' concerns.
The proposal is a complete failure.

items.x: Far from being the dispassionate arbiter it claims to be, the regulator has, by its own admission, relied almost entirely on data supplied by the very firms it oversees.
items.p: What is the speaker's point?
o: The regulator collects its own data.
The firms are not regulated by law.
The regulator admits it is biased against firms.
